query: I'm new to investing and have student loans. What should I prioritize first with my savings?

recommendations.title: Complete Emergency Fund Before Increasing Investments
recommendations.summary: Prioritize building your 6-month emergency fund ($22,000) in high-yield savings before adding to investments. Your current $15,000 cash position needs $7,000 more.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: With no emergency fund, moderate debt ($38,000), and conservative risk tolerance (loss comfort 3/10), your first priority must be financial stability. Your monthly expenses of $3,800 require a $22,800 emergency fund (6 months). You have $15,000 in cash, leaving a $7,000-$8,000 gap. Without this buffer, any unexpected expense could force you to liquidate investments at a loss or accrue high-interest debt. Your current 60% cash allocation is appropriate for this phase. Hold your existing investments (VTTSX, BND) while directing new savings to a high-yield savings account (5%+ APY) until the emergency fund is complete. With $72,000 income and $3,800 monthly expenses, you have approximately $1,467/month available for savings, allowing you to complete this fund in 5-6 months.
recommendations.suggested_action: Maintain current investment positions; redirect all new savings to high-yield savings account

recommendations.title: Evaluate Student Loan Interest Rates vs Investment Returns
recommendations.summary: Analyze your student loan interest rates. If any exceed 6%, prioritize aggressive repayment over investing beyond your employer match.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: With $38,000 in debt (likely student loans given your age and occupation) and negative net worth (-$13,000), the guaranteed 'return' from paying down high-interest debt often exceeds market returns, especially for a conservative investor. Federal student loans currently range from 5.5-8.05%, while private loans can be higher. After completing your emergency fund, if any loans exceed 6% interest, allocate extra savings to debt reduction rather than increasing investments. This provides a risk-free 'return' equal to the interest rate while improving your debt-to-income ratio for future home purchase. For loans under 5%, minimum payments are acceptable while building your house down payment fund. This strategy aligns with your conservative risk profile and medium-term goal of home ownership, as lower debt will improve mortgage qualification.
recommendations.suggested_action: Review loan interest rates; prioritize paying loans >6% after emergency fund completion

recommendations.title: Maintain Current Conservative Investment Allocation
recommendations.summary: Your 40% allocation to VTTSX (target date fund) and BND (bonds) is appropriately conservative for your profile. Hold these positions.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your current investment allocation (30% VTTSX target-date fund, 10% BND bonds) is well-suited to your beginner experience level and conservative risk tolerance. VTTSX provides instant diversification across global stocks and bonds with automatic rebalancing. BND offers stability and income. Together, these represent approximately 40% of your $25,000 in assets ($10,000 invested), which is reasonable given your lack of emergency fund. As a 28-year-old with medium investment horizon, you could theoretically handle more equity exposure, but your loss comfort of 3/10 and current financial situation (no emergency fund, moderate debt) justify this conservative stance. Do not increase investment contributions until emergency fund is complete and high-interest debt is addressed. These holdings require no action - they're appropriate foundational positions that can remain as your financial situation stabilizes.
recommendations.suggested_action: Hold existing positions; no new contributions until emergency fund complete

recommendations.title: Open Roth IRA for Tax-Advantaged House Down Payment Savings
recommendations.summary: After emergency fund completion, consider a Roth IRA for down payment savings. Contributions can be withdrawn penalty-free, offering flexibility.
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Once your emergency fund is complete (6-12 months), consider opening a Roth IRA as part of your house down payment strategy. Roth IRAs offer a unique advantage for first-time homebuyers: you can withdraw contributions (not earnings) at any time without penalty, and first-time buyers can withdraw up to $10,000 in earnings penalty-free for a home purchase. With a 5-7 year horizon for your $60,000 down payment goal, a conservative Roth IRA allocation (60% bonds/40% stocks) can potentially earn better returns than a savings account while maintaining tax advantages. Contribute the annual maximum ($7,000 in 2024) if possible after emergency fund is complete and high-interest debt is managed. This strategy balances your medium liquidity needs with growth potential. However, this is a secondary priority - only implement after completing emergency fund and evaluating debt paydown strategy.
recommendations.suggested_action: Open Roth IRA after emergency fund complete; contribute for down payment goal
